tasks.note: The spec is silent on whether recording "Contradiction the person rules on" is a confirmed write like a doc cut, or direct bookkeeping like a planner's own answer-recording; I followed the established pattern (blind-plan.ts, file-decisions.ts both put UNFILED_FILE in writable, not askable) since the person's ruling is already made at that point — recording it is bookkeeping, not a new decision to confirm. Applying the same covered/contradicting separation to blind-plan.ts's docsReviewPrompt/docsCutPrompt (per the task's named finding) changes the existing per-feature post-approval doc listing, not the doc-migration job itself; I updated its existing tests in test/reconcile.test.ts accordingly rather than leaving them asserting the old conflated wording.
tasks.built: docMigrationPrompt (src/agent/phases/doc-migration.ts) now states the Pruning stage's seven rules as bold lead-ins ("Covered section." … "Nothing covered."), between the in-scope-section rule and the confirmed-writes rule. docMigrationScope's readable/writable now include UNFILED_FILE ('plan/unfiled-decisions.md', from ./unfiled-decisions), so a contradiction ruling is written straight through, no permission prompt, the same way blind-plan and file-decisions record it — only docs/** cuts still go through the askable permission prompt. Also fixed the finding: blind-plan.ts's docsReviewPrompt and docsCutPrompt no longer bucket "covered or contradicts" as one list that "can go"; a covered section is offered for removal, a contradicting one is only reported ("which side is current is the user's to say") and, when the user rules the doc is current, recorded as an unfiled decision naming the feature via Edit on UNFILED_FILE (UNFILED_DECISIONS text), leaving the spec untouched. A later task building the Migrating/Verifying stages extends docMigrationPrompt after the "Nothing covered" line and docMigrationScope's writable (e.g. adding plan/*.spec.md) rather than re-deriving this.

tasks.note: The spec is silent on where the "Built or planned" mark is kept once written; I chose a `built: true`/`built: false` front-matter line on the draft itself (parallel to `status`), since that is the one place guaranteed to survive review and approval into the Verifying stage that needs it, and added no reader for it since no task yet consumes it. SPEC_CONTRACT (assets/plugin/skills/spec-writing/contract.md) is embedded unsubstituted (its `<feature>` placeholder is left as the literal example, unlike blind-plan.ts's single-feature `.replaceAll`), since one static prompt here covers an unknown number of picks rather than one named feature.
tasks.built: docMigrationPrompt (src/agent/phases/doc-migration.ts) now states the Migrating stage's six rules as bold lead-ins ("Offered when pruning is settled." … "Reviewed as any draft."), right after the Pruning stage's confirmed-doc-writes paragraph. docMigrationScope's writable now also includes SPECS_GLOB ('plan/*.spec.md', already imported from blind-plan.ts alongside the new PLAN_DIR import), so a migrated draft is written straight through like UNFILED_FILE, no permission prompt — only docs/** cuts still go through one. mode-setup.ts's 'doc-migration' case now composes new SpecContract(workspaceRoot) alongside its ScopeGuard, the same way 'plan' does, so a Write/Edit to plan/*.spec.md is checked against the spec contract and off-contract problems ride back on the tool result for the model to fix in the same turn. The "Built or planned" mark is carried as a `built: true`/`built: false` front-matter line on the draft itself, written by the model as part of the file it composes (no parsing code added — nothing reads it yet; a later task building the Verifying stage, which needs to tell a built feature's clean check from a planned one, reads it from there rather than inventing a new place to keep it). A later task extending the Verifying stage reads that front-matter field and the drafts this stage writes, rather than re-deriving where the mark lives.

tasks.name: Verifying a migrated feature against the code
tasks.text: What the check against the code means for a spec written from a doc about code that already exists.
tasks.note: The spec leaves the board's granularity open where a scenario mixes a satisfied rule with a disagreeing one; I resolved it at the scenario/task level (deriveBoard's existing unit), not per rule: a brand-new task is tests-only only when none of its delivered rules were ever named `on` a non-withdrawn decision, otherwise it builds normally like any other task - so "only what disagrees gets built" holds per scenario, matching how tasks are already structured, without splitting a scenario's rules across two tasks. "Check on approval" needed no new branching: a migrated spec is an ordinary `plan/*.spec.md`, so `checkDue`/`startCheck`/`approveSpec` already route it through the same check with no special case; I proved that by showing the built-spec instructions still name the single, same decisions file. I did not touch implement.ts: `how` already rides to the implementer verbatim through the existing `detail(task)`, so the "add tests only" instruction needed no new prompt wiring there. I left `feature-build.ts`'s `followAmendment` (board re-derivation after a mid-build spec amendment, with no check) on the `built=false` default, since that path runs without a check or decisions and none of the four rules describe it.
tasks.built: SpecState (spec-file.ts) now carries `built: boolean`, read from the front-matter `built:` line by new `builtOf(text)`, alongside the existing `status`/`body`. deriveBoard (tasks-file.ts) takes two new optional params, `built = false` and `decisions: Decision[] = []`; a brand-new task for a scenario whose delivered rules none of the (non-withdrawn) decisions name gets `how` set to the new exported `TESTS_ONLY_HOW` constant, which `detail(task)` (task-board.ts, unchanged) already surfaces to the implementer verbatim. reconcilePrompt (reconcile.ts) gained a paragraph telling the check, for a spec whose front matter marks `built: true`, to ask whether the code already does each rule and to report an unsatisfied one as an ordinary decision rather than build it. chat-view-provider.ts's buildFromSpec now reads the decisions file and passes `spec.built` and the decisions through to deriveBoard, so production wiring matches the tested function. A later task needing "is this spec migrated built behaviour" reads `SpecState.built`; one needing "does this scenario still disagree" reads a task's `how === TESTS_ONLY_HOW` or re-derives from decisions' `on` lists, rather than inventing a new marker.
